stewart_read: This is the classic 'hello objection' territory — customer declines in the first seconds. The rep does not use the scripted small-ask language verbatim but the outcome (non-argumentative pivot) matches the strategy.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would say the rep simply ignored the objection; the stronger read is the rep treated it as noise and redirected to the existing-estimate hook, which is strategy-consistent.
coaching_implication: Reinforce that this instinct — not arguing an early 'not interested' — is correct and worth naming explicitly to the rep as a repeatable move.

quote: Well, yeah, looks like we do still have that solar estimate built out for you.
stewart_read: Customer reveals a prior estimate exists but claims he didn't know it was for solar panels — a confusing disclosure the rep does not probe (what estimate, from whom, when). This is a Stewart observation of missed competitive/context intel, not a scored schema category miss.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have judged the confusion as low-value noise and moved straight to the more productive design/savings question at 00:57, which is what actually unlocked the real objection.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to spend 5-10 seconds clarifying what the 'estimate' was before moving on — in this call it didn't cost the outcome, but on a messier call it could leave ambiguity for the closer.

quote: I had a few guys come by with Iron Solar before, and and they told me how my house is positioned directly in sunlight.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers that his lot has direct, unobstructed sun exposure with no trees blocking it — a strong qualifying signal for panel output. This is a Stewart-flagged enthusiasm signal, not tied to a specific schema line item.
coaching_implication: Rep never reflects this back or anchors on it. A one-line acknowledgment ('that's great, unobstructed sun is exactly what maximizes savings') would have reinforced the customer's own case for solar heading into the appointment.

quote: I'm kinda sold on it, but I ain't convinced her yet.
stewart_read: Customer self-identifies the real blocker unprompted. The rep's response at 01:39-01:46 treats this correctly — folding the wife into the appointment rather than trying to close the customer solo on the phone.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read might ask why the rep didn't explicitly confirm the wife will be present on the call at the exact time slot; the transcript never gets a direct verbal confirmation from the customer that she will join.
coaching_implication: Praise the reframe move, but flag that the rep never got an explicit 'yes, she'll be on the call too' — the appointment assumes her presence without confirming it, which is a real gap for the closer to know about.

quote: Well, I got you down for tomorrow at 10AM. So I'll send you a confirmation text with the, anytime of the meeting, and then we'll see you guys then.
stewart_read: Day and time were locked, but several button_up sub-elements are missing: no one_hour_block_stated, no no_driving_at_computer instruction, no explicit is_that_fair_handshake, and the text_followup_promise is vague ('anytime of the meeting') rather than a specific tieback.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the call ran under four minutes and the customer was cooperative throughout, so the rep may have judged a lighter button-up sufficient; but the schema treats these as required elements regardless of rapport level.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to run the full button-up checklist even on easy, cooperative bookings — the one-hour block and no-driving instruction directly affect show-rate per the schema's own coaching note.

quote: Yeah. That's a goal, man. If they can convince her, then I'm sure it's a goal.
stewart_read: Customer's own language frames his wife's buy-in as an open condition of the appointment succeeding, not a settled fact. The booking is real but carries this stated contingency.
coaching_implication: This should be flagged in the handoff so the closer knows the wife is not yet sold and the appointment's actual job is to convince her, not just walk through numbers with an already-aligned couple.
